harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set audit=1 as a persistent kernel boot parameter on node1 by adding GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1" to /etc/default/grub (the cloud-image grub.d override only touches GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT, so this survives it), regenerated grub.cfg with update-grub, then performed the mandatory single-node restart to prove persistence: captured pre-reboot boot_id/health baseline, issued systemctl reboot, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (real restart, not just a service bounce), and verified post-reboot that /proc/cmdline contains audit=1 and dmesg shows the kernel audit subsystem actually enabled, with systemctl is-system-running healthy.
actions_performed: Inspected /proc/cmdline, /etc/default/grub, and /etc/default/grub.d/50-cloudimg-settings.cfg on node1 to find the correct persistence point
Edited GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX to "audit=1" in /etc/default/grub (avoids being overridden by the cloud-image grub.d file, which only sets GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT)
Ran sudo update-grub and confirmed grub.cfg linux entries include audit=1
Captured pre-reboot boot_id and systemctl is-system-running baseline
Issued sudo systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Verified changed boot_id, /proc/cmdline containing audit=1, dmesg audit-enabled messages, and healthy systemctl is-system-running post-reboot

evidence.requirement: audit=1 configured persistently in bootloader config
evidence.summary: Found cloud-image grub.d override of GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT, so set GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1" in /etc/default/grub instead; ran update-grub and confirmed both grub.cfg linux entries now include audit=1
Captured baseline boot_id (f9bf293d...) and systemctl is-system-running=running before reboot
systemctl reboot issued in background; command returned immediately with the launched PID before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: changed boot identity proving a real restart
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable immediately after reboot (connection reset), then came back with a new boot_id (4d3dcf68...) differing from baseline, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: audit=1 persisted across reboot and audit subsystem active post-restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline contains audit=1; dmesg shows 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' and audit_enabled=1; systemctl is-system-running=running confirms node health recovered
